definition: After Time Out — a set play a coach draws up during a timeout, usually designed to get a specific shot for a specific player.
When a player scores a basket while being fouled and earns one extra free throw. The classic three-point play.
A cut behind a defender toward the basket, used when the defender overplays or denies the passing lane.
An aggressive ball-screen coverage where two defenders trap the ball handler, forcing the ball out of their hands.
Sprinting from help position to contest a shooter, under control, with high hands and a balanced base.
Dribble Hand-Off — the ball handler dribbles toward a teammate and hands the ball off, often using their body as a screen.
A pick-and-roll defense where the screener's defender sags back toward the paint, protecting the rim while the guard fights over the screen.
The corners of the free-throw line where it meets the lane — a prime catch-and-shoot and playmaking spot.
An off-ball screen set away from the ball, freeing a shooter to pop out toward the sideline for a catch-and-shoot three.
When the screener fakes setting a screen and slips to the basket or pops before contact, punishing defenses that over-commit.
Pass to a teammate and immediately cut to the basket for the return pass — the simplest two-man action in basketball.
A ball-screen coverage where the screener's defender jumps out high to briefly contain the ball handler before recovering.
The half of the court away from the ball. Help-side defenders sag into gaps, ready to rotate and protect the paint.
A side pick-and-roll coverage that forces the ball handler away from the screen and toward the baseline, with the big containing the sideline.
In help rotations, the defender closest to the baseline on the weak side — responsible for tagging the roller and protecting the rim.
The spot at the middle of the free-throw line — a key help position and a common place to catch against zone defense.
The first pass after a defensive rebound that starts the fast break — quick, accurate, and up the court.
The rectangular lane area near the basket. Touching the paint with the dribble collapses the defense and creates open shots.
A two-man action where a teammate screens the ball handler's defender, then rolls to the basket — the most-run action in modern basketball.
The area near the elbow extended, a few feet outside the lane — a common spot for entry passes and split actions.
A bounce pass threaded between two defenders to the rolling big in pick-and-roll — the fundamental read against drop coverage.
A shot fake that lifts the defender off the floor, creating a driving lane or drawing a foul.
The big who sprints straight to the rim in transition, ahead of the defense, for early deep catches.
A legal block set by an offensive player without the ball to free a teammate — the foundation of pick-and-roll and off-ball actions.
The area above the elbows near the top of the key — a common spot for ball handlers to attack from and for skip passes to target.
A pick-and-roll with a back screen set on the roller — the screener's defender gets screened, freeing the roller or creating a three-point look.
Two off-ball screens set in succession for the same cutter or shooter — hard to guard without switching.
When a help defender briefly bumps or 'tags' the rolling big to slow them down before recovering to their own man.
The side of the court opposite the ball — where help defenders position themselves and where skip passes attack.
A DHO flowing directly into a ball screen — the guard gets the hand-off and immediately uses a second screen.
